questions.title: Synaptic fatigue results from neurotransmitter depletion
questions.subject: neuro
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Physiology > Nerve and Muscle Physiology > Synaptic Transmission
questions.question: What is the fundamental physiological cause of synaptic fatigue (exhaustion) at a repeatedly, rapidly stimulated synapse?

options.B: Depletion of the presynaptic terminal's readily releasable neurotransmitter stores
options.C: Complete lack of oxygen reaching the nerve terminal
options.D: Massive local accumulation of lactic acid

explanations.A: Incorrect. Postsynaptic receptor inactivation is not the principal mechanism of synaptic fatigue; the limiting step is presynaptic, not postsynaptic.
explanations.B: Correct. With sustained high-frequency stimulation, vesicle mobilization and release cannot keep pace with demand, so the presynaptic terminal's readily releasable neurotransmitter pool becomes depleted, and each successive action potential releases less neurotransmitter, weakening the postsynaptic response. Fatigue in this sense is protective, preventing a synapse from firing indefinitely, and it resolves once the terminal has time to replenish its vesicle stores.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Local hypoxia is not the described mechanism of synaptic fatigue in this context; the fatigue is a presynaptic neurotransmitter-supply phenomenon, not an oxygen-delivery one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lactic acid accumulation is a feature of fatigued skeletal muscle metabolism, not the mechanism of synaptic fatigue at a nerve terminal.

questions.learning_objective: State that synaptic fatigue (exhaustion) after repetitive stimulation is caused chiefly by depletion of presynaptic neurotransmitter stores, not by receptor damage or oxygen lack.
